Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: The _____ was 1492 decree expelling Jews from Spain.
Alhambra Decree.fact: The Alhambra Decree (also called the Edict of Expulsion; Spanish: Decreto de la Alhambra, Edicto de Granada) was an edict issued on 31 March 1492 by the joint Catholic Monarchs of Spain, Isabella I of Castile and Ferdinand II of Aragon, ordering the expulsion of unconverted Jews from the Crowns of Castile and Aragon and its territories and possessions by 31 July of that year.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: Over half of Spain's Jews had converted as a result of the religious persecution and pogroms which occurred in _____
Alhambra Decree.fact: Over half of Spain's Jews had converted as a result of the religious persecution and pogroms which occurred in 1391.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: Due to continuing attacks, around 50,000 more had converted by _____
Alhambra Decree.fact: Due to continuing attacks, around 50,000 more had converted by 1415.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: The decree was then formally and symbolically revoked on 16 December _____ by the regime of Francisco Franco, following the Second Vatican Council
Alhambra Decree.fact: The decree was then formally and symbolically revoked on 16 December 1968 by the regime of Francisco Franco, following the Second Vatican Council.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: This was a full century after Jews had been openly practising their religion in Spain and synagogues were once more legal places of worship under Spain's Laws of _____
Alhambra Decree.fact: This was a full century after Jews had been openly practising their religion in Spain and synagogues were once more legal places of worship under Spain's Laws of Religious Freedom.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: In _____, the government of Spain passed a law allowing dual citizenship to Jewish descendants who apply, to "compensate for shameful events in the country's past"
Alhambra Decree.fact: In 2015, the government of Spain passed a law allowing dual citizenship to Jewish descendants who apply, to "compensate for shameful events in the country's past".

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: The Spanish law expired in _____, and new applications for Spanish citizenship on the basis of Sephardic Jewish family heritage are no longer allowed
Alhambra Decree.fact: The Spanish law expired in 2019, and new applications for Spanish citizenship on the basis of Sephardic Jewish family heritage are no longer allowed.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: However, the descendants of the Jews exiled from the _____ may still apply for Portuguese citizenship
Alhambra Decree.fact: However, the descendants of the Jews exiled from the Iberian Peninsula may still apply for Portuguese citizenship.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: Under Islamic law, the Jews, who had lived in the region since at least Roman times, were considered "_____ of the Book" and treated as dhimmi, which was a protected status
Alhambra Decree.fact: Under Islamic law, the Jews, who had lived in the region since at least Roman times, were considered "People of the Book" and treated as dhimmi, which was a protected status.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: Jewish merchants were able to trade freely across the _____ world, which allowed them to flourish, and made Jewish enclaves in Muslim Iberian cities great centers of learning and commerce
Alhambra Decree.fact: Under Islamic law, the Jews, who had lived in the region since at least Roman times, were considered "People of the Book" and treated as dhimmi, which was a protected status. Jewish merchants were able to trade freely across the Islamic world, which allowed them to flourish, and made Jewish enclaves in Muslim Iberian cities great centers of learning and commerce.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: This led to a flowering of _____ culture in Spain during the Middle Ages, as Jewish scholars were able to gain favor in Muslim courts as skilled physicians, diplomats, translators, and poets
Alhambra Decree.fact: Compared to the repressive policies of the Visigothic Kingdom, who, starting in the sixth century had enacted a series of anti-Jewish statutes which culminated in their forced conversion and enslavement, the tolerance of the Muslim Moorish rulers of al-Andalus allowed Jewish communities to thrive. Jewish merchants were able to trade freely across the Islamic world, which allowed them to flourish, and made Jewish enclaves in Muslim Iberian cities great centers of learning and commerce.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: Although Jews never enjoyed equal status to _____, in some Taifas, such as Granada, Jewish men were appointed to very high offices, including that of Grand vizier
Alhambra Decree.fact: Although Jews never enjoyed equal status to Muslims, in some Taifas, such as Granada, Jewish men were appointed to very high offices, including that of Grand vizier.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: By the 14th century, most of the _____ (present-day Spain and Portugal) had been reconquered by the Christian kingdoms of Castile, Aragon, León, Galicia, Navarre, and Portugal
Alhambra Decree.fact: By the 14th century, most of the Iberian Peninsula (present-day Spain and Portugal) had been reconquered by the Christian kingdoms of Castile, Aragon, León, Galicia, Navarre, and Portugal. Alhambra Decree.fact: By the 14th century, most of the Iberian Peninsula (present-day Spain and Portugal) had been reconquered by the Christian kingdoms of Castile, Aragon, León, Galicia, Navarre, and Portugal. Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: During the _____ re-conquest of Iberia, the Muslim kingdoms in Spain became less welcoming to the dhimmi
Alhambra Decree.fact: The Reconquista, or the gradual reconquest of Muslim Iberia by the Christian kingdoms in the North, was driven by a powerful religious motivation: to reclaim Iberia for Christendom following the Umayyad conquest of Hispania centuries before. By the 14th century, most of the Iberian Peninsula (present-day Spain and Portugal) had been reconquered by the Christian kingdoms of Castile, Aragon, León, Galicia, Navarre, and Portugal.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: In the late 12th century, the _____ in al-Andalus invited the fanatical Almohad dynasty from North Africa to push the Christians back to the North
Alhambra Decree.fact: In the late 12th century, the Muslims in al-Andalus invited the fanatical Almohad dynasty from North Africa to push the Christians back to the North.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: Many Jewish people fled to other parts of the Muslim world, and also to the _____ kingdoms, which initially welcomed them
Alhambra Decree.fact: During the Christian re-conquest of Iberia, the Muslim kingdoms in Spain became less welcoming to the dhimmi. In the late 12th century, the Muslims in al-Andalus invited the fanatical Almohad dynasty from North Africa to push the Christians back to the North.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: In Christian Spain, _____ functioned as courtiers, government officials, merchants, and moneylenders
Alhambra Decree.fact: After they gained control of the Iberian Peninsula, the Almohads offered the Jews a choice between expulsion, conversion, and death. In Christian Spain, Jews functioned as courtiers, government officials, merchants, and moneylenders.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: Therefore, the _____ community was both useful to the ruling classes and to an extent protected by them
Alhambra Decree.fact: Many Jewish people fled to other parts of the Muslim world, and also to the Christian kingdoms, which initially welcomed them. Therefore, the Jewish community was both useful to the ruling classes and to an extent protected by them.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: As the _____ drew to a close, overt hostility against Jews in Christian Spain became more pronounced, finding expression in brutal episodes of violence and oppression
Alhambra Decree.fact: As the Reconquista drew to a close, overt hostility against Jews in Christian Spain became more pronounced, finding expression in brutal episodes of violence and oppression.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: In the early fourteenth century, the _____ kings vied to prove their piety by allowing the clergy to subject the Jewish population to forced sermons and disputations
Alhambra Decree.fact: In Christian Spain, Jews functioned as courtiers, government officials, merchants, and moneylenders. As the Reconquista drew to a close, overt hostility against Jews in Christian Spain became more pronounced, finding expression in brutal episodes of violence and oppression.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: Thousands of Jews sought to escape these attacks by converting to _____
Alhambra Decree.fact: Thousands of Jews sought to escape these attacks by converting to Christianity.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: These Jewish converts were commonly called conversos, _____ nuevos, or marranos; the latter term was used as an insult
Alhambra Decree.fact: These Jewish converts were commonly called conversos, Cristianos nuevos, or marranos; the latter term was used as an insult.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: These suspicions on the part of _____ were only heightened by the fact that some of the conversions were insincere
Alhambra Decree.fact: By the mid-15th century, the demands of the Old Christians that the Catholic Church and the monarchy differentiate them from the conversos led to the first limpieza de sangre laws, which restricted opportunities for converts. These suspicions on the part of Christians were only heightened by the fact that some of the conversions were insincere.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: Some conversos, also known as crypto-Jews, embraced _____ and underwent baptism while privately adhering to Jewish practices and faith
Alhambra Decree.fact: Some conversos, also called crypto-Jews, embraced Christianity and underwent baptism while privately adhering to Jewish practices and faith.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: For their part, the _____ community viewed conversos with compassion, because Jewish law held that conversion under threat of violence was not necessarily legitimate
Alhambra Decree.fact: Some conversos, also called crypto-Jews, embraced Christianity and underwent baptism while privately adhering to Jewish practices and faith. For their part, the Jewish community viewed conversos with compassion, because Jewish law held that conversion under threat of violence was not necessarily legitimate.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: Although the _____ was also officially opposed to forced conversion, under ecclesiastical law all baptisms were lawful, and once baptized, converts were not allowed to rejoin their former religion
Alhambra Decree.fact: Although the Catholic Church was also officially opposed to forced conversion, under ecclesiastical law all baptisms were lawful, and once baptized, converts were not allowed to rejoin their former religion.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: Before the Spanish expulsion, the Jews had been expelled from England in _____, several times from France between 1182 and 1354, and from some German states
Alhambra Decree.fact: Before the Spanish expulsion, the Jews had been expelled from England in 1290, several times from France between 1182 and 1354, and from some German states.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: The French case is typical of most expulsions: whether the expulsion was local or national, the _____ usually were allowed to return after a few years
Alhambra Decree.fact: Before the Spanish expulsion, the Jews had been expelled from England in 1290, several times from France between 1182 and 1354, and from some German states. The French case is typical of most expulsions: whether the expulsion was local or national, the Jews usually were allowed to return after a few years.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society

Alhambra Decree.fact: Before the Spanish expulsion, the Jews had been expelled from England in 1290, several times from France between 1182 and 1354, and from some German states. Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: Their marriage in _____, which formed a personal union of the crowns of Aragon and Castile, with coordinated policies between their distinct kingdoms, eventually led to the final unification of Spain
Alhambra Decree.fact: Their marriage in 1469, which formed a personal union of the crowns of Aragon and Castile, with coordinated policies between their distinct kingdoms, eventually led to the final unification of Spain.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: Although their initial policies towards the Jews were protective, _____ and Isabella were disturbed by reports claiming that most Jewish converts to Christianity were insincere in their conversion
Alhambra Decree.fact: Although their initial policies towards the Jews were protective, Ferdinand and Isabella were disturbed by reports claiming that most Jewish converts to Christianity were insincere in their conversion.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society
Alhambra Decree.question: As mentioned above, some claims that conversos continued to practice _____ in secret (see Crypto-Judaism) were true, but the "Old" Christians exaggerated the scale of the phenomenon
Alhambra Decree.fact: As mentioned above, some claims that conversos continued to practice Judaism in secret (see Crypto-Judaism) were true, but the "Old" Christians exaggerated the scale of the phenomenon.

Alhambra Decree.subject: Indian Society

Alhambra Decree.fact: Although their initial policies towards the Jews were protective, Ferdinand and Isabella were disturbed by reports claiming that most Jewish converts to Christianity were insincere in their conversion. Alhambra Decree.fact: By 1492, Ferdinand and Isabella had won the Battle of Granada and completed the Catholic Reconquista of the Iberian Peninsula from Islamic forces. Although Isabella was the force behind the decision, her husband Ferdinand did not oppose it.
